description: The Global Tailings Portal is a free, searchable database of mine tailings storage facilities built and hosted by GRID-Arendal in collaboration with the Investor Mining and Tailings Safety Initiative, co-chaired by the Church of England Pensions Board and the Swedish National Pension Funds' Council on Ethics, with support from UN Environment. It was launched in January 2020 after the Brumadinho dam collapse, from disclosures that more than 100 listed mining companies made to investors. The home page counted 1,805 tailings storage facilities at 692 mine sites of 297 operators on 26 September 2026. Each facility has location, ownership, status, year of first operation, raising method, height, current and planned impoundment volume, independent review date, consequence-of-failure hazard class and answers on downstream impact and climate assessments. Access is through a map, overview and analysis pages and a search tool; bulk data are available on request from GRID-Arendal, and a downloadable Excel and CSV release is announced but not yet offered. No licence is stated on the portal. Caveats: the data are self-reported by companies, cover mainly publicly listed firms, and the provider calls the site a beta still being verified; the global number of tailings dams is estimated at 3,500 to 33,000. For simulation it supports hazard exposure and cascading-failure studies of dam breaches affecting downstream infrastructure. Related catalogue records include the WISE Uranium chronology of tailings dam failures and the USGS Mineral Resources Data System.
